author: Metanart
quote:
Well, I’m kinda disappointed.

For a "game of the millennium" that everyone kept hyping up, this new GTA feels rather bland and toothless compared to its predecessors. The dialogue is tedious and dull, the characters are uninteresting, and there’s an overall sense of restriction regarding what you can and cannot do in an *open-world* game.

I have some issues with the new limitations - like the fact that you can’t steal every vehicle or kill every NPC - not to mention the idiotic karma system. It’s bizarre to see this in a GTA game; it makes you wonder- why are you even allowed to kill cops? Isn't that "bad" too? Why does the game decide for me what’s right or wrong, effectively dictating how I’m "supposed" to play? Sure, there are plenty of new mechanics, but they don’t actually make the gameplay any more engaging. 
As a game, it’s... fine, I guess- I’d rate it higher if it hadn’t been hailed as the greatest game in history. But as it stands? It’s just ok-ish game with some pros and cons. Definitely not worth the full price, and it’s certainly not the Game of the Millennium, lol.

And as for the main characters - they evoke nothing but antipathy, both of them equally. "Dumb and Dumber" - that’s the perfect description for them.

And once again, 30 FPS on the latest, supposedly powerful consoles? I have an Xbox Series X, and this isn’t even funny anymore - it’s just really bad. On my PC, almost all games have been running at 100+ FPS for a long time now. After playing on PC, trying to play new games on a console at 30 FPS just feels absurd.

author: Metanart
quote:
I finished the whole DLC in 3 days - including all secret bosses.

And I strongly disagree with the inflated ratings it received. It could be 6 of 7 out of 10, no more.

First - in this DLC nothing is being told about Melina or any other characters from the main game. I became a Frenzy lord -and Melina promised to kill me. DLC says nothing about that. The story itself is not good for me. It just exists - I suppose that I missed again some item descriptions to realize genius ideas - but I don't care much - I'm tired of this laziness of FromSoftware.

The quests system is the same garbage as before - go somewhere, do smth and maybe you will receive... something. It was fun in Dark Souls - that was some kinda of a feature. It was fine in Lovecraft-like Bloodborne.

But for open-world games like Elden Ring, where you're missing a huge part of quests just because you can't find someone or forget about something - because you don't have a proper journal - ooooh, that's not good.

All the "hardness" of new bosses is in fact that they are faster than the previous ones, and have longer combos.

Copy-pasted weapons like katanas from Sekiro or Claws from BB, enemies from Bloodborne - like Winter Lanterns and so on.

The overall content of the DLC - you're again just travelling around absolutely empty locations and grabbing some new weapons and a huge stack of COOOKBOOOKS. It's Ubisoft-tier game design - not a game I can enjoy - it's just content I can consume.

On Xbox, in performance mode - I'm catching freezes during some boss fights - super nice for the Souls game.

The final of the DLC is disappointing - not a proper cutscene, just some ultra-small nothing. I killed almost a god for a minute. And got nothing in the end.

Designers are doing good as usual - some locations are quite beautiful.

Summary - FMPOV it's quite lazy-crafted DLC and even for fans of Souls I'm not sure that it's worth buying for full price.
game_title: Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree

author: Metanart
quote:
To be honest, for once, not the worst, but quite drawn-out plot, which really ends in stupidity

Good gameplay that is fun at first, but the closer the end-game gets, the worse and more boring and it gets

Terrible drop rate of things compared to the previous parts. Boring, repetitive dungeons, with a lot of backtracking again and again and again and boring end game activities (3 actually) and forced multiplayer that doesn't work

PVP just broken and is not working like - at all, seriously.

All online activity in the game is to gather in 10 players togeher a couple of times a day and kill the world boss - after which all players again disperse to farm mobs alone or in a pair with a friend - no more.

And for some reason, a lot of different mechanics that already existed in d2 and d3 were not implemented - because of this, the game feels poor - no legendary potions, no runes, no class rifts, no different types of goblins - it is extremely strange why the experience of previous games was ignored in 4th part

If you get it at a discount it's ok. For the full price, I would not recommend.

LOL, updated to zero after 1.0.1 patch

Blizzard managers are clearly increasing the time that is tedious to spend on the game, so that the battle pass probably does not close too quickly

Screw them =)

author: Metanart
quote:
I have not played Assassins for a long time, and decided to buy them because I like the theme of the Vikings

Pros:

Interesting introduction and the first hours of the game, cool voice acting of Eyvor-guy and in general - a pleasant main character

Minuses:
Outdated wooden graphics, looks frankly bad against the background of more modern games

Absolutely pointless side quests that cause nothing but facepalm, and seem to be 10-year-olds

Unfortunately - a stupid plot, interesting only at the beginning and becoming more boring further

Tons of grind and constant artificial stretching of gameplay, even in story missions

I tried to score on all the side missions and go strictly according to the plot, but at some point I just could not stand the meaninglessness of the actions that move the plot progress

The whole game resembles stupid and meaningless crap, in the process I constantly caught myself thinking - "why am I now doing what I am doing, and why should I not give a **** about these characters"
